prerequisites: Solid basic knowledge of solid mechanics
Ability to present and communicate one's own solutions to given problems
Social skills, e.g., for possible collaboration in small teams
Successful completion of the Study Introductory and Orientation Phase (StEOP)

learning_outcomes.text: Possess basic knowledge of the theory of the topics mentioned below in the field of multibody system dynamics.
Ability to implement and apply the learned theoretical principles to practical problems (e.g., from mechatronics, vehicle dynamics, robotics).
Analytical and synthetic thinking for model building and interpretation of numerical simulation results of (mechatronic) problems.
Ability to critically question the correctness and interpretability of one's own numerical solutions to problems determined by computer.
General understanding of the theoretical background of multibody system programs and their use for effective modeling of technical systems.
Describe the foundations of the theory of the mentioned topics in multibody system dynamics concisely.
Confidently apply the taught theoretical principles to practical problems in mechatronics, vehicle dynamics, and robotics.
Critically analyze model building assumptions and numerical simulation results for mechatronic problems.
Methodically examine the correctness and interpretability of one's own numerical solutions determined by computer.
Clearly explain the theoretical background of multibody system programs.
Purposefully apply the theoretical background of multibody system programs for effective modeling of technical systems.
Structure the kinematics of multibody systems with rigid and deformable bodies.
Correctly formulate Newton-Euler equations, d’Alembert's, Jourdain's, and Gauss's principles, and the derived equations of motion.
Apply the mentioned equations and principles to typical examples with computational proficiency.
Professionally solve application examples from mechatronics, vehicle dynamics, and robotics using a selected multibody dynamics software package and interpret results with justification.
Independently structure complex problems.
Explain one's own solutions, assumptions, and limitations comprehensibly and discuss them with peers.
Constructively discuss peer feedback on drafts and results.
Present complex content, models, and results in an audience-appropriate manner.
Discuss alternatives for modeling and validation strategies, taking into account environmental and professional conditions.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics and dynamics of multibody systems with rigid and flexible bodies.
Representation and transformation of motion variables via generalized position coordinates/velocities. Absolute and relative coordinates.
Degrees of freedom of position and velocity.
Holonomic and non-holonomic, scleronomic and rheonomic systems. Ideal joints and constraints.
Systematic construction of equations of motion via d’Alembert's and Jourdain's principles with application examples. Gauss's principle. Derivation and application of Gibbs-Appell equations.
Topology in multibody systems. Procedure for kinematically closed loops.
Application examples from mechatronics, vehicle dynamics, and robotics and their numerical treatment (simulation) using a selected multibody dynamics software package.
teaching_methods: Guidance and assistance in practical implementation
Independent solving of engineering problems using a common multibody dynamics software package at a computer workstation

assessment_methods.method: Written and/or oral examination on theoretical principles
Review and documentation of independently developed exercise tasks at the computer workstation
